engine: markdown
title: "Parquet"
---

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

Files ending in `.parquet` or `.pq` are read and written with
[nanoparquet](https://nanoparquet.r-lib.org/), no flags needed. Parquet stores
data by column, compressed and with its types, so it is smaller and faster to
read than CSV.

## Writing

Point `--output` (`-o`) at a `.parquet` file, or use `rush convert`:

```{term}
rush convert -o mtcars.parquet mtcars.csv
ls -l mtcars.csv mtcars.parquet
```

## Reading

```{term}
rush run 'dplyr::filter(df, mpg > 25) |> dplyr::select(mpg, cyl, hp)' \
  mtcars.parquet
```

## With SQL

`rush sql` lets DuckDB read Parquet files directly, so a query on a large file
doesn't load the whole file into memory:

```{term}
rush sql "SELECT cyl, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(mpg), 1) AS avg_mpg
          FROM mtcars
          GROUP BY cyl
          ORDER BY avg_mpg DESC" mtcars.parquet
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv mtcars.parquet
```
